picked.t: ‘고물가 장기화’ 베트남, 10월에도 5% 물가상승 지속…연료가격 상승 영향
picked.body: 베트남 호치민시의 한 슈퍼마켓. 올 들어 베트남에서 고물가가 장기화되고 있는 가운데 지난달에도 5%대 물가 상승이 지속된 것으로 나타났다. 베트남 재무부 통계국(NSO)이 3일 내놓은 ‘2026년 10월 사회경제적 현황 보고서’에 따르면, 지난 10월 베트남의 소비자물가지수(CPI)는 전월 대비 0.2%, 전년 동월 대비 5.09% 상승했다. 이에 따라 10월 기준 CPI는 전년 동기 대비 4.57% 상승했다. 지난 10월 한 달간 CPI는 전월과 비교해 전체 구성요소 11개 상품·서비스군 가운데 4개군을 제외한 7개군이 상승했는데, 주로 국제 유가에 따라 베트남 국내 석유제품 가격이 함께 오른 데 주로 기인했다. 자세히 살펴보면, 전월 대비 2.86% 오른 교통운송 부문을 제외하면, 나머지 6개군은 0.04~0.39% 범위의 상승을 나타냈다. 지수가 하락한 4개군은 △식품·외식(-0.35%) △의류·모자·신발(-0.01%) △정보통신(-0.19%) △문화·오락·여행(-0.57%) 등이었다. 1~10월 평균 CPI는 지난해 같은 기간보다 4.57% 올랐는데, 이 중 식품·외식은 4.61% 올라 전체 CPI를 1.65%포인트 끌어올렸고, 주거·전기·수도·연료·건설자재가 6.66% 올라 1.51%포인트를, 교통운송이 6.98% 올라 0.70%포인트를 기여했다. 특히 교통운송 가운데 연료 가격이 13.09% 큰 폭으로 올랐다. 나머지 품목군도 모두 올랐다. 기타 상품·서비스가 4.72%, 음료·담배가 3.80%, 교육이 3.29%, 가정용품·설비가 2.88%, 문화·오락·관광이 2.75%, 의류·모자·신발이 2.04%, 의약품·의료서비스가 1.19%, 정보통신이 0.12% 상승했다. 에너지·의료비·교육비 등 국가가 관리하는 품목과 가격변동성이 높은 식품을 제외한 근원 CPI는 10월 전월 대비 0.05% 내렸으나, 전년 동월 대비로는 4.04% 올랐다. 10월 기준 평균 근원 CPI는 4.24% 상승해 전체 CPI 상승률을 밑돌았다.

picked.t: Korean men marry Japanese women in record number as K-culture's pull in Japan grows
picked.body: The figure, released Nov. 5 by the Ministry of Data and Statistics, formerly Statistics Korea, is the highest since the government began compiling the statistics in 2008, Korea JoongAng Daily reported. A total of 21,399 multicultural marriages, those involving a foreign or naturalized spouse, were registered in 2025, down 0.2% and the first decline in four years. With total marriages went up 8.1% to 240,326, the multicultural share accounts for nearly nine in every 100 marriages. Unions with Vietnamese women fell 5.8% to 5,409, with Chinese women dropped 5.2% to 3,224, and those with Thai women 8.8% to 1,960. The popularity of Korean entertainment in Japan, helped by streaming platforms, is believed to be a major factor behind the rise. "The influence of Korean culture, including K-dramas, appears to be contributing to a continued rise in favorable attitudes toward Korea," a Data Ministry official said, as cited by the paper. Marriages between Korean men and Japanese women have more than doubled since 2022, rising from 615 that year to 848 in 2023 and 1,188 in 2024, Seoul Economic Daily reported. Their share of multicultural marriages doubled over the period, from 3.5% to 7%. The narrowing economic gap between the two countries has also been cited. South Korea's per capita gross national income overtook Japan's in 2023 and 2024 before slipping back below it in 2025, at $36,963 against an estimated figure in the low $38,000s for Japan, according to the Bank of Korea. Some observers also point to gender tensions in South Korea, including the spread of derogatory terms aimed at both men and women. In Japan, Tokyo Shimbun reported in late September that female membership at Moa Love, a Tokyo matchmaking agency that pairs Japanese women with Korean men, had doubled from a year earlier. About 40% of its Korean male members do not speak Japanese, though translation apps have eased the language barrier, the newspaper said. One woman, a 38-year-old IT freelancer in Tokyo given the pseudonym Kana, told the newspaper that she hears "saranghae," or "I love you," every day and that the Korean men she has dated walk on the traffic side of the street. "Once you've dated a Korean man, Japanese men honestly fall short," she said. Aya, 36, who married a Korean man in April, yet told the newspaper that not every man is as gentle as those in K-dramas, and that she chose her husband regardless of nationality. In South Korea, births to multicultural families fell 0.5% to 13,347 in 2025, or 5.2% of all births, while marriages involving naturalized citizens dropped 9% to 2,076. A ministry official told Korea JoongAng Daily that a fall in naturalizations in 2021 and 2022, when the Covid-19 pandemic made citizenship procedures more difficult, had reduced marriages involving naturalized citizens, which appeared to have contributed to fewer births after a time lag. Multicultural divorces rose 1.4% to 8,104, even as divorces nationwide fell 3.3%, lifting their share of all divorces to 9.2% from 8.8%. A ministry official said the slight rise appeared to reflect the growth in multicultural marriages over the past few years.
